items.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995
items.q: I think he and Tony Bennett are the only two musicians of the older ranks whose voices are better now

ctx.x: Not professionally tough times, no. I fact I don’t know any tough times. Basie saw him off. Basie came up and introduced him on his first single job, which was in Boston, and he went out for a while with Sweets in a group, Jerome Richardson and Sweets, and a wonderful group of musicians. And he always seemed to have work, we never had any bad years that I can remember. So I think he’s done real well. And actually he seems to be getting better and better. Everybody thinks his voice is still wonderful.
Well I told you that I think so. I think he and Tony Bennett are the only two musicians of the older ranks whose voices are better now then they were when they were younger. Maybe Mel Torme, maybe.

Yes, Mel— I think you could put Mel in there certainly. He’s wonderful. But I think also that they have become, this sounds ridiculous to say at Joe’s age, but they’ve become more sophisticated in their presentation. Joe is now much more than a singer. When he was with Basie, you know, his sort of trademark was that he would come on very serious, and just stand there and sing. You know he never did all this snapping and nodding. Now he’s developing a rapport with the audience and he takes the mic and he goes up…
